title: When can I plant or move a rose?

common.applies_to: Hybrid Tea, Floribunda or Grandiflora bush rose; answer to a common question
common.preserved_uncertainty: Planting months differ by country and climate (C-3): the UK source gives late autumn or late winter to early spring, and cold-winter US sources prefer or require spring. New Zealand months come from garden centres only, and May in Australia from one source. Three New Zealand sources speak of roses in general, not bare-root roses. For potted roses two New Zealand pages still give a best season. Sources differ on the best point in the dormant season to move a rose (C-9).

content.heading: When can I plant or move a rose?

items.text: Plant a bare-root rose (one sold without soil on its roots) while it is dormant, with no leaves, between late autumn and early spring. One source says to avoid the middle of winter when the ground is frozen.
In New Zealand, winter is the best time to plant a rose, and planting can go on through spring. One garden company says June and July are the best months. Months are only a guide.
In Australia, plant a bare-root rose in June or July. One source says planting can start in May. Months are only a guide.
In the UK, plant a bare-root rose while it is dormant, between October and early March. Months are only a guide.

In the US, where winters are very cold, spring is the preferred time to plant bare-root roses. One source puts the line at winters that fall below -10 °F, and says that where it stays warmer than that, autumn or spring both work.
A rose in a pot can be planted over a longer season than a bare-root rose. UK and New Zealand sources say all year, and two US sources say through the growing season.
items.limit: One source says not to plant into frozen or very dry ground. Another says to keep it well watered if you plant in spring or summer. One New Zealand source says autumn or winter is still the best time.

items.text: Move an established rose while it is dormant, which means it is not actively growing. Most sources say winter. Some say late autumn or early spring.

In New Zealand, one garden centre says to move a rose in July, after pruning and once the risk of frost has passed. One garden company says June or July. Months are only a guide, because frosts vary from year to year.
A rose can be moved in the growing season if you have to. It will need extra watering afterwards.
